## Computational biologist studying protein isoform stability

I am a Ph.D. candidate in the Korkin Lab at Worcester Polytechnic
Institute. My research combines bioinformatics, machine learning, and
structural biology to understand how alternative splicing affects
protein stability and disease.

I develop computational methods for analyzing protein isoforms and
validate their predictions using structural, evolutionary, and
experimental evidence.

[Download my CV](files/SenbaoLu_CV.pdf){.btn .btn-primary}
[Explore my research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## Research interests

- Alternative protein isoforms
- Protein stability and molecular dynamics
- Machine learning for biological prediction
- Structural bioinformatics

## Current status

I expect to graduate in Fall 2026 and am interested in postdoctoral involving computational biology, bioinformatics, and machine learning.

Outside computational biology, I travel around the world for food and classical music.
